Isn't this commit just a refactor ? Can it just be a refactor?

> Isn't this commit just a refactor ?

no, the collection needs to be by association, currently it looks like it is just returning everything.

currently:

```
collection_util::getCollectionMembers(
                    asyncResp,
                    boost::urls::format("/redfish/v1/Systems/{}/Memory",
                                        BMCWEB_REDFISH_SYSTEM_URI_NAME),
                    interfaces, "/xyz/openbmc_project/inventory");
```

this patch:

```
 collection_util::getCollectionByAssociationById(
        asyncResp,
        boost::urls::format("/redfish/v1/Systems/{}/Memory", systemName),
        systemName, systemPath, boardInterfaces, "containing", dimmInterfaces,
        nlohmann::json::json_pointer("/Members"));
```

> Can it just be a refactor?

yse, it can probably be split into 2 patches

- extracting the inline `BMCWEB_ROUTE` handler to a separate function (refactor)
- changing over to query by association, or branch between new way / old way depending on the meson option, for systems which do not have the association.
Done

My question here: If i have a multi-host system and my system name is `system` (same as the default value on the meson option) and i have managed host interface, i will not get any memory collection.

Is this intended?

I thought in multi-host case we simply ignore the meson option for the system name.

I have no idea what we do with the meson option, I just put a safe guard here, to not use 'system' as system name in a multi host system, because even though it can happen, it shouldn't happen, therefore I placed the condition.

And I got this review:
https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/bmcweb/+/83978/comment/3b5369fa_14e9f86b/

https://github.com/openbmc/bmcweb/blob/2ca561945f9c518e4916cd23c194f89816fdbeee/redfish-core/include/utils/systems_utils.hpp#L29

I don't think we need this condition, if we can drop it the code will be simpler.
